analysis.title: Carlisle Companies Inc. (CSL) 3Q26 Recap: Steady Re-Roof Activity, Cost Actions, and Price Realization Continue, Allowing for Upside to Margins Over Time
key_insights: Carlisle reported 3Q26 adj. EPS of $5.92 vs GS estimate $5.90 and FactSet consensus $5.89. Revenue rose 8.6% vs GSe +4.8%, adding $0.21 to EPS, partly offset by an adj. EBIT margin of 20.5%, 63bps below GS's model, which cost $0.18.
Other EPS bridge items for the quarter: taxes and net interest expense +$0.02 each, share count ($0.04), one-time adjustments ($0.01).

CCM (Carlisle Construction Materials) revenue rose 8.4% YOY vs GSe +5.4%, on re-roof demand, pricing and strategic initiatives. CCM EBITDA margin fell 200bps YOY to 28.2% vs GSe 29.0% as negative price/cost more than offset productivity and operating leverage.
CWT organic sales grew 9.4% YOY vs GSe +3.1% on share gains and weather-driven roof coatings demand, offsetting weak new construction. CWT EBITDA margin rose 60bps YOY to 18.0% vs GSe 19.8%.

GS sees potential for meaningful upward revisions to sales and margins as conditions stabilize. Drivers: new product momentum, cost actions (management cited 500bps of CWT expansion masked by record diesel prices), and re-roof activity GS views as fairly resilient to the macro.

In CCM, re-roof demand was up mid-single digits, offsetting a similar decline in new construction. Channel inventories normalized after a modest 2Q pull-forward, with strength holding into October. GS expects low-single-digit 4Q volume growth.
GS models 4Q segment sales up 8.7% in CCM and 7.9% in CWT, 4Q consolidated sales growth of 8.5%, full-year 2026 +5.8% and 2027 +5.9% (CCM +6.7%, CWT +3.7% in 2027).
Management said 9 of 12 new products have been launched this year and the rest are on track, targeting 25% of total sales from products introduced in the last 5 years.
Rising diesel and freight costs pushed price/cost parity out by one quarter. 2027 is expected to be price/cost positive if energy and freight hold at current levels.

Price realization: CCM +4% in 3Q with a +7% guide for 4Q, CWT +3%. CCM had three price increases this year and CWT two, including one in October, plus freight surcharges. Costs were up double digits in 2Q, high-teens in 3Q, and are expected up mid-to-high teens in 4Q.

GS looks for incremental relief in MDI and polyols costs in coming quarters as force majeures lift. It models price up low-single digits in each segment in 2027, with price/cost tailwinds peaking in 2Q27 before tougher comps.
GS forecasts 4Q adj. EBITDA margin of 26.8% in CCM (flat YOY) and 16.8% in CWT (up 95bps). For 2027 it models margin expansion of 92bps in CCM and 146bps in CWT.

Balance sheet: net debt/EBITDA 1.8x (1.4x a year ago), $547mn cash, 3Q FCF from continuing operations $277mn, capex on track for $180mn (down from $200mn), $350mn buybacks in the quarter with the full-year buyback guide holding at $1.2bn. Management sees bolt-on M&A opportunities in building envelope.
GS models FCF of $802mn in 2026 (about 15.1% of sales, consistent with guidance) and $909mn in 2027.

GS estimate changes: 2026 EPS $21.05 from $21.10, 2027 $24.70 from $24.45, 2028 $29.15 from $28.30. Price target to $480 from $464, based on 14.5x (from 15.0x) Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA. Buy rating maintained; the lower multiple reflects limited visibility on inflation and price/cost.
Scenario analysis: upside case $524 (19.4x 2027 EPS), downside case $291 (13.1x 2027 EPS). GS sees favorable risk/reward at $345.21, 39.0% upside to the target.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised to $480 from $464 on 14.5x Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA (was 15.0x). GS expects margin upside from cost actions, price realization and new products, and sees the 4Q guide and 2027 estimates as potentially conservative.

sector_views.rationale: Re-roof demand is steady and fairly resilient to the macro, offsetting weak new construction. Carlisle is positioned to take share as contractors value its labor- and time-saving products.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 adj. EPS $5.92 reported (adjusted) vs GS estimate $5.90 and FactSet consensus $5.89. Revenue +8.6% YOY vs GSe +4.8%. Adj. EBIT margin 20.5%, 63bps below GS's model.
CCM 3Q26 revenue +8.4% YOY (GSe +5.4%), EBITDA margin 28.2%, down 200bps YOY (GSe 29.0%). CWT organic sales +9.4% YOY (GSe +3.1%), EBITDA margin 18.0%, up 60bps YOY (GSe 19.8%).
GS 4Q forecasts: consolidated sales +8.5%, CCM sales +8.7%, CWT sales +7.9%, CCM adj. EBITDA margin 26.8% (flat YOY), CWT 16.8% (up 95bps YOY).
Management guides for CCM price +7% in 4Q, capex of $180mn in 2026 and $1.2bn of share repurchases for the year.
risk_factors: Raw material cost increases that cannot be passed through.
Failure to execute on strategic initiatives, including closing and integrating announced acquisitions.
Productivity and efficiency efforts fall short of expectations.
Loss of, or change in order patterns from, key customers.
Increased competition from newer entrants seeking share.
Limited visibility on energy, diesel and freight costs and the path for price/cost.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects cost actions, price realization and new products to lift margins, with CWT cost actions largely complete and a masked 500bps of CWT expansion per management. It models 92bps of CCM and 146bps of CWT margin expansion in 2027 and sees the 4Q guide and 2027 estimates as potentially conservative.
tension_points.bear_case: 3Q margins missed expectations. CCM EBITDA margin fell 200bps YOY and CWT came in below GS's 19.8%, because negative price/cost from diesel, freight and raw materials (costs up high-teens in 3Q) outran pricing. Price/cost parity slipped one quarter.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy and freight costs that do not ease, so 2027 price/cost does not turn positive, or raw material costs that cannot be passed through.

theme_stances.key_argument: Price realization is coming through, and price/cost tailwinds should follow once energy and raw material inflation eases.
theme_stances.evidence: we expect price/cost tailwinds should energy prices decline
